name: Study of an Author/Writer in Focus
description: The objective of the module is to provide an in-depth study of one writer/theorist or thinker. The course will focus on the works or even one text of the selected writer and attempt to understand the trajectory of his/her thought in detail. This year we focus on Nietzsche. We begin at a key turning point in the corpus, which is the moment after Zarathustra. We then look at genealogy and beyond good and evil--as two texts representing a turning point in his trajectory. We then enter into the debate about his unpublished fragment, famously centered on the controversial 'will to power' fragments. ' the course then takes a backward turn: we look at his unfinished 'philosopher's notebooks, ' daybreak, (some reference to gay science), human all too human, untimely meditations--with the grand finale which is the young Nietzsche as prodigy, birth of tragedy. The remainder of the course is dedicated to Heidegger on Nietzsche--we look at all the Heidegger material and talk about its enormous influence on all of modern thought, including that of Deleuze and Foucault. We will also take especial care to think of the image of antiquity in Nietzsche (and compare it to Hoelderlin and Heidegger).
